_comment: Card CB-Q leg C — the 12 h 305-station / 2-signal / 300 s arm.
WHY 300 s IS DEFENSIBLE HERE, against the standing NO-GO: the 1 h probe
(runs/cbq305_2f_1h_d10) measured the carry prediction VALID on THIS posture —
D5 v2 σ̂₀ = 1.17x (raw σ̂₀² = 1.364) against the 6.54x that condemned the tier on
the full multi-signal posture, and 2.44 %/epoch refloats (94.8/ep on 3886
carried DDs) against the 33 %/ep that gave arc life ~15 min.  Two signals per
satellite is a far smaller DD population and it changes the answer.
⚠ AND WHY THAT PROBE CANNOT CLEAR IT: both known 300 s failure modes are LATE.
The D5 storm was measured to be STEADY-STATE, not warm-up (project_dev300s_tier
records an 11-epoch smoke reading 463 flags/ep as the ambiguous case that a long
run had to discriminate), and the deg-15 SH field runaway to 2620 TECU happened
over hours 4.1-4.7.  A 13-epoch probe is inside neither.  This arm exists to
cross hour 4 with the counters armed.  If the a₀₀ physical-band WARN fires or
D5 σ̂₀ climbs, the tier is refused for this card and 60 s (epoch_decimation_n 2,
the validated tier) is the fallback — that is the pre-registered stop rule.
WHAT IT MEASURES FOR THE CARD: the emitted OSB structure function has log-log
slope ~1.0, i.e. the signal lives at LONG lags — which is precisely what a
decimated tier can measure (the tier rule allows emission/datum mechanics and
forbids convergence/arc physics).  Lags from 300 s up are directly comparable to
the 30 s arms; nothing below 300 s is available and nothing below it is claimed.
⚠ NO 30 s DENOMINATOR AT THIS SCALE: a 12 h 305-sta 30 s arm is ~9.3 h of wall.
Cross-tier per-epoch metrics are NOT compared (project_dev300s_tier's standing
rule); the SF at shared lags is, and it is the only cross-tier claim made.
One knob vs _cbq305_2f_1h_d10: duration.  FRESH lineage; own paths.
